judgments.reasoning_cat1: The all-caps notice states the claims-made-and-reported trigger and defense-costs-erosion in definite terms, with no vague operative term beyond the incorporated "pursuant to the terms herein."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It tracks Insuring Agreement I and Section V.A on defense costs eroding the limit; no contrary provision found, though such notices are sometimes played against the Awareness Provision in VI.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording is a standard validation clause; the only oddity is the trailing comma and the requirement of "another duly authorized representative" after officers already signed, which is definite enough to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in the Declarations and does not conflict with the Alteration clause VIII.K's endorsement-signature requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional consideration and reliance preamble; "all information provided to the Insurer" is broad but is defined out by the Application definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with VIII.B, which likewise makes application statements the basis of the Policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is garbled ("made against any Insured by or on behaif Employee") and turns on the vague reporting standard "as soon as practicable," both of which affect what the coverage grant actually requires.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 60-days-after-expiration outside limit must be squared with VI.C's 60-days-after-the-Claim rule and with Section V.A's deeming of Claims first made under a prior policy, a live source of tension.
judgments.clause_name: I. Insuring Agreements — A. Wrongful Employment Act

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The extension is carefully bounded by "solely by reason of" and expressly excluded for the spouse's own wrongful acts; the domestic-partner sentence is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with the definitions of Insured Individual and Loss, which it expressly borrows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The categories (estates, heirs, legal representatives, assigns) are enumerated and the carve-back for the representatives' own acts is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It harmonises with the Bankruptcy clause VIII.I and the Insured Individual definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It grants the ERP only where "the insurer chooses not to renew or the Parent Company cancels," leaving unaddressed the case of insurer cancellation for nonpayment permitted by VIII.C.2, and contains the run-together "by the insuredand."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The election right sits alongside VIII.J, which excepts ERP notice from the Parent Company's agency, and with V.A's limit-sharing rule; the trigger gap against VIII.C.2 is a genuine fit question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is a sweeping catch-all — "any other such documents submitted in connection with the underwriting" plus "any publicly available documents" filed with the DOL or EEOC — whose reach against the enumerated items is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It feeds VIII.B's representations clause and the entire-agreement sentence in VIII.K, which arguably pulls the other way on incorporated documents.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "any other payment to or for the benefit of an employee arising out of the employment relationship" is a broad residual sitting after specific items, and "non-deferred cash incentive compensation" is the only stated exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates with Loss exclusions 4 and 6 and Exclusion IV.B.1; those uses are coherent with this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition; "implied employment contract" is broad but is a recognised legal category rather than an ambiguity of drafting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interlocks with Exclusion IV.A.4 and IV.B.3 on contractual liability, which limit recovery rather than contradict this definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "a written demand against any Insured for monetary or non-monetary relief" and the "similar formal proceeding"/"similar document" catch-alls give the trigger date genuinely contestable boundaries, and this is exactly the sort of term insurers and insureds read differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with the Potential Claim definition (III.R), the Awareness Provision VI.A and the deemed-one-Claim rule in V.A, which together decide whether an earlier demand fixes the Claim outside this policy period.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable and necessary legal fees and expenses" is a familiar vague standard, and the parenthetical carve-out of Insureds' own compensation is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with V.A (defense costs erode the limit) and V.C (no Defense Costs without consent).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is broad but definite: any violation of statute, regulation, ordinance or common law concerning employment discrimination anywhere in the world.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits Wrongful Employment Act (III.X), Other Workplace Tort's tail requirement and Exclusion IV.A.5's Retaliation carve-back.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list uses shifting qualifiers — labor "directed by" versus "directed solely by," and contractors only if they work "solely for" the Policyholder — making the class boundary contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps imperfectly with Insured Individual (III.J), which admits contractors and leased persons only on a written indemnity, and with III.V excluding independent contractors' Third Party Claims.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 3, "illegal work related harassment," is an open-ended residual after two specifically sexual limbs, raising an ejusdem generis question about how far it reaches.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used consistently in III.X and in the Other Workplace Tort tail; no contrary provision appears.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-element definition with nothing to construe beyond the terms it cross-references.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with III.J and III.O throughout the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The conditional limbs 4 and 5 ("only if prior to any Claim ... agreed in writing to indemnify") are precise, though "functional equivalent" in limb 1 is somewhat open.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits in tension with the broader Employee definition (III.G), which brings the same contractors and leased persons in without any indemnity condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "common nexus" and "causally or logically connected" are notoriously elastic phrases whose application to a group of claims is regularly disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its consequences run through Exclusion IV.A.2(b) and V.A's single-Claim aggregation, so a broad reading can swallow the coverage grant in Section I.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The grant expressly includes "front pay and back pay" while carve-out 4 excludes the "future salary, wages ... of a claimant who has been or shall be ... reinstated," a boundary that is hard to draw on the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Carve-out 9 excludes Punitive Damages but Item 6 of the Declarations elects punitive coverage, and the proviso restores it, so the pieces must be read together with IV.B and V.A.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The numbering is defective (two items numbered around 3 and 5, so the list's items cannot be cleanly identified) and limb 2's "adequate employment related policies and procedures" is vague.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The closing "but only when alleged as part of a Claim for" tail ties it to the other defined offences and is coherent with III.X.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to Item 1; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Item 1 names FINRA, so the reference is complete and consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite composite definition; the debtor-in-possession clause is explicit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with III.U (Subsidiary), VIII.A.3 and the Bankruptcy clause VIII.I.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The wording is short and clear on its face; the defect is the cross-reference to "Section VII.C," as Section VII is Notices and cancellation appears at VIII.C.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That mis-citation means the definition points to a non-existent termination provision, so it must be reconciled by inference with VIII.C.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extremely broad but written as an open list ("without limitation") plus a second sentence sweeping in noise and electromagnetic fields, so the residual's reach is uncertain though deliberately maximal.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in Exclusion IV.A.7, with a Retaliation carve-back; no inconsistency with the rest of the policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "an allegation or accusation ... provided such allegation does not constitute a Claim, but subsequently may give rise to a Claim" defines the term by reference to what it is not, leaving a genuinely blurred line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The boundary against III.D (Claim) and the operation of VI.A determine which policy period bears the loss, so the two definitions must be read against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definite: punitive or exemplary damages plus named statutory liquidated damages.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with Loss carve-out 9 and Item 6's election of punitive coverage, which the proviso in III.L expressly accommodates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "illegal retaliatory treatment of Employees, including any" makes the four limbs illustrative rather than exhaustive, so the class is open, though "illegal" anchors it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Retaliation carve-backs in IV.A.5 and IV.A.7 depend on this definition and are coherent with it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Numerical thresholds are precise; the trailing "solely with regard to Wrongful Acts occurring at or after the time such entity became a Subsidiary" is grammatically awkward but its sense is recoverable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cross-refers to VIII.A.1, whose 10%/110% employee thresholds are themselves confusingly drafted, so the acquisition mechanics require harmonising.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "is, or attempted to be, a customer or vendor" is an odd and imprecise formulation, and the exclusion of independent contractors' claims sits against an otherwise broad class.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Independent contractors can be Employees under III.G and Insured Individuals under III.J.5, so the carve-out here needs reconciling with those definitions and with Exclusion IV.A.9.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A pure aggregation of two defined terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with III.X and III.Z as used in Section I.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 3, "any other persons for whom the Insureds are legally responsible," is a general residual whose scope beyond the enumerated actors is uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with Section I's coverage grant and with the definitions it aggregates.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Limb 4's "adverse change in the terms, conditions or status of employment" is a broad residual after specific job actions, and "wrongful" is repeated redundantly across limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It fits the Wrongful Employment Act definition and the wrongful-termination carve-back in IV.B.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The protected-characteristic list ends with "or on any other basis prohibited by law," a classic catch-all whose reach beyond the enumerated grounds is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It works with III.V and Item 7's election of Third Party Claim coverage without evident inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The repeated "in any way involving" preambles and the "including any other ... statute or law similar to any statute or law described in (a) through (h)" tail are open-ended residuals of a kind commonly litigated for scope.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion A.1 and A.2 (prior notice, pending or prior claims, Interrelated Wrongful Acts) cut against Section I's grant for Wrongful Acts "before or during the Policy Period" and against V.A's deeming rule, requiring careful harmonisation.
judgments.clause_name: IV.A. Exclusions Applicable to All Loss

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Item 4's "any request order (including the cast of compliance with such order) or agreement for nan-monetary relief" is garbled and the residual "any other equitable remedy" is open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The defense-costs-only treatment of equitable relief must be read with Claim III.D.1.a, which expressly includes demands for non-monetary relief, and with Loss's definition.
judgments.clause_name: IV.B. Exclusions Applicable Solely To Loss other than Defense Costs

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are numerically definite, but the deeming rule turns on "the same Wrongful Act and/or all Interrelated Wrongful Acts" and on notice "under this Policy or any prior policy," which imports the elasticity of III.K.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Deeming a Claim first made under a prior policy can defeat the trigger in Section I and overlaps with Exclusion IV.A.1 and IV.A.2, a relationship a court would have to work through.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: the Insurer pays only above the Item 4 retention, borne by the Insureds.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with V.C's 50%-of-retention consent carve-out and with Item 4 of the Declarations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "which shall not be unreasonably withheld" and "unreasonably refuse to consent" are open standards, and the bar on incurring any Defense Costs without consent sits awkwardly beside the Insurer's own duty to defend.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The consent bar and the hammer clause must be read with the Defense Costs definition and with V.A's exhaustion rule; the interplay is coherent but tight.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming language is workable, but it depends wholly on the vague boundary of "Potential Claim" and its closing sentence about pre-Claim fees is terse.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be reconciled with Section I's requirement that the Claim be first made during the Policy Period and with III.D/III.R's overlapping definitions.
judgments.clause_name: VI.A. Awareness Provision — Notice of Potential Claim

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The required contents are itemised in definite terms; the only defect is the corrupted numbering of the second limb.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with VI.A and with VIII.H's compliance condition precedent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "as soon as practicable" is a vague standard, though the 60-day outside limit is precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Its 60-days-after-the-Claim deadline differs from Section I's 60-days-after-policy-expiration deadline, so which governs a post-expiration Claim noticed under VI.A requires construction.
judgments.clause_name: VI.C. Awareness Provision — Notice of Subsequent Claim

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming sentence is internally odd: notices are effective on actual receipt "or one day following the date such notices are sent, whichever is earlier," which can deem receipt before it happens.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It governs notices required by Section I, VI and VIII.C and is otherwise consistent with Item 11's addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly mangled — a missing subparagraph label, "as for a period of ninety (90) days" — and the 10% cap in the first paragraph sits confusingly against the 110% trigger in the next, so the acquisition rule's operation is genuinely unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It must be squared with the Subsidiary definition III.U, which cross-refers back to VIII.A.1, and with VIII.A.3's run-off for former Subsidiaries; the thresholds leave a gap for acquisitions between 10% and 110%.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The substance (reliance, severability of the Application, limited imputation) is definite, but the lettering is corrupted and a stray "m" precedes the second half.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Making the Application "part of this Policy" sits in mild tension with VIII.K's entire-agreement sentence, and it interlocks with the Application definition III.A.
judgments.clause_name: VIII.B. Representations and Severability with Respect to Application

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The mechanics are numerically precise, though two paragraphs are both numbered 5 and "short fate basis" is a typo for short-rate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the provision the Policy Period definition should have cited, and it pairs with II.C's ERP triggers, which do not cover insurer cancellation for nonpayment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence makes the Policy excess only for Third Party Claim loss, while "in all other events, this Policy is intended to provide primary insurance" is hortatory rather than operative.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against Item 7's election of Third Party Claim coverage and Section I.B, the excess/primary split is workable but the "intended to" sentence invites argument about layering.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single definite sentence extending the Policy worldwide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It matches the worldwide references in III.F, III.Q and IV.A.5 and conflicts with nothing.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Specific currency, source of exchange rate and conversion date; nothing genuinely ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Items 3 and 4 of the Declarations and the Loss definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard subrogation wording; "everything necessary" is broad but conventional and bounded by the stated purpose.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No provision waives subrogation or conflicts; it fits VIII.H's compliance condition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "full compliance with all the terms of this Policy" as a condition precedent is a sweeping requirement, and the sentence contains an evident typo ("the Insureds' ability" for liability).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the notice conditions in Section I and VI rather than contradicting them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One definite sentence preserving both parties' positions on insolvency.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with III.O's debtor-in-possession language and VIII.A.2's receiver provision.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The agency is stated with an express carve-out for ERP notice; wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out dovetails with II.C, which gives the Policyholder or Insured Individuals the ERP election, so the pieces cohere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clauses are definite, though the last sentence's blanket no-waiver/no-estoppel language operating in both directions is unusually broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The entire-agreement sentence sits against VIII.B, which incorporates the Application as part of the Policy, and against the Declarations' listed endorsements.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate headings clause with no operative uncertainty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It slightly complicates reliance on section headings elsewhere but conflicts with no provision.
